text:
The deafening street howled around me.

Tall, slender, in mourning, with a queenly sorrow,

A lady passed, who with sumptuous gesture

Gathered, swaying, the folds of her veils,


Most agile and noble, with two marble legs.

Suddenly I drank, with a madman's spasm,

And in her livid gaze, center of a thousand tempests,

The pleasure that annihilates, the paralyzing honey.


A lightning flash. Night. Fugitive beauty

Whose gaze made me, in one blow, be born again.

Except in eternity, shall I never see you again?


In any case far away, too late, perhaps never!

For I do not know where you fled, nor do you suspect my route,

You whom I would have loved. Oh you, who knew it!

translation.title: To a Passerby
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the famous instant of urban encounter: lightning, loss, and impossible recognition.
